page.title: Audiovisual Production for Biotech Events: What to Decide First
page.description: A practical guide to roles, run of show, rehearsal timing and escalation paths for biotech webinars, summits and hybrid conferences.
page.h1: Audiovisual Production for Biotech Events: What to Decide First
page.definition: Audiovisual production for biotech events is the end-to-end crew, equipment and workflow that turns scientific presentations into reliable live and on-demand streams, covering run of show ownership, speaker rehearsals, backup streams and compliance-ready recordings.
page.quick_answer: Assign a single show caller, lock the run of show two weeks out, schedule one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before the event, and confirm a backup stream and escalation contact before the agenda is final.

sections.h2: Who owns the run of show and the backup stream?

blocks.p: One named show caller must own the run of show and the backup stream; without that ownership, cues slip and failover never triggers.

ul: Show caller writes and maintains the run of show document
Platform operator monitors the primary and backup encoders
Speaker manager confirms slide decks and lower-thirds match the run of show
Escalation contact (usually the scientific lead) approves any on-the-fly changes

sections.h2: What roles does a biotech summit need versus a webinar?

blocks.p: A simple webinar runs with one producer; a summit or hybrid conference needs a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator at minimum.

head: Event type
Minimum crew
rows: Show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator
All summit roles plus on-site camera crew and venue AV liaison

sections.h2: When do you schedule the full rehearsal and the technical check?

blocks.p: Run one full rehearsal on the actual platform two to five days before the event, then a 60-minute technical check immediately before going live.

ol: Lock speaker slides and videos four days before rehearsal
Rehearse every transition, Q&A hand-off and backup-stream switch
Record the rehearsal for speaker review
Technical check: verify audio, encoder health, lower-thirds and closed captions

sections.h2: How do you handle compliance, branding and recording deliverables?

blocks.p: Biotech events need branded lower-thirds, closed captions, a compliant edited recording and short clips delivered within 24 to 48 hours.

ul: Branded slide template and lower-thirds approved by communications
Live captions fed to the platform and saved in the recording
Edited master recording with speaker names, affiliations and disclaimers
Two to three social clips cut to 60-90 seconds each
Backup stream recording stored for 90 days

sections.h2: What escalation path covers speaker failures or platform outages?

blocks.p: Define a three-tier escalation path before the agenda is final so the show caller never improvises during a live incident.

ol: Tier one: platform operator restarts encoder or switches to backup stream
Tier two: show caller pauses agenda, cues holding slide, alerts speaker manager
Tier three: scientific lead and communications lead approve agenda changes or cancellation

faq.q: How much does produced AV for a biotech webinar cost?
faq.a: A moderated webinar production typically ranges from $2,500 to $7,500 per production; summits and hybrid conferences start around $10,000 and scale with crew size and venue needs.

faq.q: What lead time should I plan for a virtual summit?
faq.a: Allow six to eight weeks from kickoff to live date; a repeat webinar format can move in three to four weeks if the run of show and speaker briefs are already standardised.

faq.q: Which platforms work well for produced biotech events?
faq.a: Productions run on the platform you already use such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard; the crew adapts to the platform rather than forcing a new tool.

faq.q: Who provides the backup stream and encoder?
faq.a: The production crew brings a hardware encoder and a secondary streaming destination; the platform operator monitors both and switches on the show caller's cue.

faq.q: When do I get the edited recording and clips?
faq.a: Delivery within 24 to 48 hours after the event ends, while attendees still remember the content and compliance review is fresh.
